name: preempt-rt-mmci-threaded

change.description: Keep the PREEMPT_RT MMCI handler threaded, but disable preemption while its board-specific one-sector PIO loop fills the FIFO.

constant_contract.kernel: Linux 5.15.211-rt97 ARM NOMMU FDPIC XIP from QSPI
constant_contract.data: VFAT on the same SD card at approximately 1.95 MHz
constant_contract.latency: TIM3 CH1 PB4/D3 hardware reference to priority-99 SCHED_FIFO kthread PG7/D4 response

deployment.verification: U-Boot accepted the staged CRC before update and verified the programmed QSPI image CRC during the subsequent clean boot.

storage_probe.operation: write and sync 256 KiB, drop caches, read and hash, delete and sync
storage_probe.interpretation: The post-drop-cache hash does not match 256 KiB of zeroes, and the block layer reported many failed data sectors plus a failed FAT metadata write.

runtime_priority_followup.change: Set irq/35-mmci-pl18x to SCHED_FIFO priority 98, immediately below rt_scope at priority 99.
runtime_priority_followup.observation: Sync and fsck still returned block write I/O errors at sector 2048.
runtime_priority_followup.conclusion: Ordinary IRQ-thread dispatch priority is not the only lost hard-IRQ semantic.

hammer.reason: A full workload would further damage FAT and could not produce valid SQLite durability results.

decision: Retain this negative result. Test a board-opt-in compatibility mode that keeps the MMCI primary handler unthreaded and restores raw-spinlock serialization, then quantify its unavoidable interrupt-off cost with the physical scope.
interpretation: Preventing higher-priority task preemption during the FIFO fill and raising the MMCI IRQ thread both failed. The STM32F746 workaround depends more broadly on the original hard-IRQ execution and lock semantics.
